legal_rules_infrastructure.detail: Governed Ruleset/Rule/Source/TestCase/EngineRun schema and lifecycle (src-tauri/src/legal_rules.rs), a constrained-DSL rule interpreter (10 safe operators, no code eval/network/filesystem), and a Settings UI for authoring/testing/approving rulesets. Contains zero Israeli substantive law - a ruleset is only usable once a lawyer has sourced, tested and approved it. Phase B (Medical/Wage/Liability evidence ledgers) and Phase C (the first real lawyer-approved legal module) are deliberately not attempted.

legal_rules_infrastructure_hardening.detail: All 6 P0 findings and 5 of 6 P1 findings from the 2026-08-25 independent audit fixed and covered by new regression tests: terminal-state immutability (approved/superseded/revoked, not just approved), required non-empty reviewer identity on approve/review, page-level (not version-level) source grounding for approval, engine_kind always read from the ruleset itself, effective-period validation and enforcement, deterministic priority/rule_key tie-breaking, atomic single-transaction approval, forward-only engine-run status, exact integer arithmetic for cent-valued comparisons, and rejection of meaningless (assertion-free) test cases. P1-6 (linking legal_engine_runs to legal_deadlines/damage_calculations via FK) is deliberately deferred until real integration work begins, per the audit's own recommendation. cargo test --locked: 58/58 at the time; confirmed on real Windows CI at run #14, commit d7b3ae6.

phase_b_matter_profile.detail: First milestone (B1) of the Phase B roadmap: a matter_profile 1:1 side table and a matter_parties contact list, plus a Rust-side allowlist tightening create_matter/update_matter's case type. The existing matters table is never ALTERed - src-tauri/src/matter_profile.rs and its migration explain why. Plain office-management data: no lock/approval lifecycle, no DB immutability triggers, since none of it is an evidentiary claim. The original shape (event_date/court_name/a single contact_details blob, case types motor_vehicle_accident/workplace_accident/.../generic_civil) was confirmed on real Windows CI at run #15, commit 16a31b3. A design review then prompted fixes applied in place (before any client-use database depended on the original shape): event_date/court_name renamed to primary_event_date/primary_court_name (room for a matter's many dates/proceedings); contact_details replaced with structured display_name/entity_kind/identifier/phone/email/address fields; the case-type taxonomy renamed/widened to traffic_accident/work_accident/general_negligence/medical_malpractice/civil_commercial/generic_civil/other (generic_civil kept for backward compatibility); matter_parties.role's DB CHECK dropped in favor of Rust-only validation. This review-fix commit (6e89cd0) was confirmed on real Windows CI at run #16 - 66/66 tests passed on the real runner. B2-B6 (Workstreams, Missing Evidence Matrix, Medical/Wage/Liability Ledgers, AI Pipeline, Case Health) remain deliberately unattempted - each gets its own planning pass before implementation; the review also refined that roadmap (B5 splits into B5a focused-retrieval before B5b AI-ledger-proposals; B3's requirements read as office-policy, not statutory; B4's ledger items use a draft/verified/superseded/stale lifecycle) without changing any shipped code.

phase_b_workstreams.detail: Second milestone (B2) of the Phase B roadmap: a matter_workstreams table (medical/liability/wage/insurance/btl/negotiation/litigation, each not_applicable/not_started/active/blocked/done) auto-seeded from a matter's case type at creation via a new workstreams::reconcile function, called inside the same transaction as create_matter's INSERT (now wrapped in conn.transaction() for the first time) and update_matter's UPDATE when matterType actually changes (update_matter now SELECTs the old value first to detect a real change). reconcile is idempotent and non-destructive: it inserts any of the 7 kinds not yet present, then upgrades an existing not_applicable row to not_started only if the new case type's defaults include it - an already not_started/active/blocked/done workstream is never touched. list_matter_workstreams calls reconcile first (read-repair) before listing, so a pre-B2 matter with zero workstream rows gets backfilled transparently on first view. Kind/status are Rust-only validated (no DB CHECK), matching matter_profile.rs's own pattern. Matter Pack defaults are office-workflow defaults, not legal determinations - freely overridable per matter. New tab 'מסלולי עבודה' in MatterWorkspace.tsx (WorkstreamsTab.tsx); a case-type <select> was added to the existing edit-matter modal so a lawyer can actually trigger a case-type change. 9 new backend tests (seeding, reconcile-never-touches-active, backfill-on-list, kind/status validation, cascade delete, plus 3 pure unit tests) - 75/75 total. cargo check/test --locked, npm run build, contract:check (94/94, no drift), qa:static (now also checking oneTableInMatterWorkstreams) all pass. Migration re-verified idempotent via direct sqlite3 (applied 3x): 41 tables, 28 indexes, 37 triggers, user_version=15, integrity ok, fk_check clean. This commit has not yet had its own Windows CI run. B3-B6 remain deliberately unattempted, each still pending its own planning pass.

phase_b_requirements.detail: Third milestone (B3) of the Phase B roadmap: a matter_requirements checklist table (13 typical document keys - id_document/police_report/medical_records_initial/medical_records_full_file/wage_stubs/employer_incident_report/witness_statements/insurance_policy/btl_forms/vehicle_photos/expert_opinion/contract_document/correspondence_records - each not_applicable/not_collected/requested/collected/stale) built to the exact same shape and reconcile idiom as B2's matter_workstreams: one idempotent, non-destructive requirements::reconcile function called from create_matter, from update_matter on a real case-type change, and as read-repair in list_matter_requirements. Deliberately no linked_document_id column in this pass - wiring a requirement to a specific document (an 'open source' button, a staleness cascade off scanner.rs) has no consumer yet and would be a speculative, unused column; status stays entirely lawyer-driven, including 'stale', since what that should mean for a checklist item isn't yet defined by real usage. New tab 'ראיות חסרות' in MatterWorkspace.tsx (MissingEvidenceTab.tsx), structurally identical to WorkstreamsTab.tsx. The original shape (86/86 tests) was shipped at commit 94f7c63. A user code review then found a genuine semantic gap: priority was computed only from the matter's current case-type Pack, so a requirement the lawyer manually collected outside the Pack (or one whose Pack membership changed after collection) could surface as status=collected next to priority=not_applicable - a self-contradictory read, even though the underlying reconcile/status-preservation logic never touched the row incorrectly. Fixed in place (no migration - schema unchanged, still user_version=16/42 tables/29 indexes/37 triggers) by splitting the read-model into two fields, both still computed at read time and never persisted: relevance (applicable/not_applicable - whether the key currently belongs to the Pack, or the lawyer has otherwise acted on it) and priority (required_by_office_policy/recommended/optional - only meaningful when relevant, Option<String> now instead of overloading not_applicable as if it were a priority tier). A key in the current Pack keeps the Pack's priority; a key outside the Pack still at status=not_applicable is relevance=not_applicable/priority=None; a key outside the Pack that the lawyer has moved to not_collected/requested/collected/stale becomes relevance=applicable/priority=optional, so a lawyer's own action never produces a contradictory display again. 3 new tests (2 unit tests on the split function, 1 integration regression test reproducing the exact reported scenario) plus updated assertions on the existing seeding test - 89/89 total. cargo check/test --locked, npm run build, contract:check (96/96, no drift), qa:static all pass. linked_document_id and manual-only stale remain deliberately deferred, reaffirmed by the same review as still correct. This review-fix commit has not yet had its own Windows CI run. B4-B6 remain deliberately unattempted, each still pending its own planning pass.
